resources.title: The Vision of the Redemption of the Dead
resources.speaker: M. Russell Ballard
resources.description: President Ballard recalls the losses Joseph F. Smith endured and invites us to study the revelation he received. Doctrine and Covenants 138 describes Christ commissioning messengers to carry His gospel to the dead.
resources.sourceEvidence: D&C 138:30–34, 50–52; discussion of Joseph F. Smith’s bereavements and the Savior’s ministry.

resources.title: Trust in the Lord
resources.speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
resources.description: President Oaks explains what scripture teaches about the spirit world and the work of salvation there. When questions remain unanswered, he counsels trust in the Lord and care in distinguishing revealed doctrine from speculation.
resources.sourceEvidence: D&C 138:30–34, 58; cautions against treating personal accounts or near-death experiences as official doctrine.

resources.title: Kingdoms of Glory
resources.speaker: Dallin H. Oaks
resources.description: President Oaks teaches about the celestial, terrestrial, and telestial kingdoms. He connects final judgment with our choices and what we become through Jesus Christ, repentance, and covenant faithfulness.
resources.sourceEvidence: Sections I–IV, especially judgments according to desires and choices, conversion, and D&C 138:57–59. Do not erase the stated exceptions or confuse universal resurrection with exaltation.

resources.title: Our Father’s Glorious Plan
resources.speaker: Weatherford T. Clayton
resources.description: Drawing on his experience as a physician, Elder Clayton speaks about birth, death, and hope in Jesus Christ. He follows the journey from the spirit world to resurrection and judgment, testifying that every person will rise again.
resources.sourceEvidence: Paragraphs on a dying widow and her daughters; spirit world; universal resurrection; judgment in 3 Nephi 27.
resources.alt: Weatherford T. Clayton speaking at general conference in April 2017

resources.title: The Redemption of the Dead and the Testimony of Jesus
resources.speaker: D. Todd Christofferson
resources.description: Elder Christofferson explains how temple service bears witness of Christ’s Resurrection and the reach of His Atonement. He makes clear that people who have died retain their agency: proxy ordinances take effect only if they accept them.
resources.sourceEvidence: Opening discussion, paragraphs on agency and acceptance; The Power of Christ’s Resurrection; The Infinite Reach of Christ’s Atonement.
resources.alt: D. Todd Christofferson speaking at general conference in October 2000

uniquenessReview.scope: All repository HTML source URLs; all assets with matching decoded dimensions. Different source poster IDs and scenes verified visually.

bookOfMormonSegmentReview.contentOverlap: Both are distinct short segments of longer Church films already linked on Watch. Exact poster images and source URLs are new; underlying footage is not entirely new.

sceneGrounding.verified: Invitation to feel hands, feet, side; each person comes forward and witnesses the risen Savior.
The afflicted are brought forward; He heals all brought to Him; healed people and others bow and worship.
He weeps, blesses children one by one, prays for them; angels then descend and minister. A blessing scene need not combine the later angel scene.
Children around Jesus; multitude kneels; Jesus kneels on earth to pray. His prayer words cannot be written, so do not invent dialogue.
Jesus teaches Beatitudes to multitude. Text does not specify a mountain position or precise archaeology.
